issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual specification declare acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int), but both the template usage (Main.java) and the provided solution implement and call a three-parameter version acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). This mismatch in method parameters can confuse students about the correct signature to implement and will cause compilation/test failures if they follow the UML instead of the examples/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter), or (B) update the template Main and the solution SealSaloon to use the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust calls accordingly. Prefer aligning the UML/text to the existing template usage (three-parameter) if tests/examples expect that form.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and description declare acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) while the repository code (and example calls in Main) implement acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch (missing supplier parameter and different parameter ordering) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the UML/description expect a 4-argument method but the template/example and solution use a 3-argument signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and explain that supplier info is not required, or (B) update the implementation (and example calls in Main) to match the UML by adding the supplier parameter: acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Ensure parameter names and ordering are consistent in problem text, template examples, and solution code.
